Sound familiar?

Too many women walk in overwhelmed. It doesn't have to be that way.

  • Not knowing which papers, accounts and dates matter until someone asks for them.
  • Paying attorney hours for questions a coach could have answered.
  • Feeling like everyone else is making the decisions.
  • Not knowing what high-conflict tactics look like until they're already happening.

Here's what you'll learn

Five things we'll cover in 60 minutes

What a divorce coach does, and what an attorney does

Who to call for what, so legal time is spent on legal work.

How to get organised before the first meeting

The documents, accounts and timeline to gather so you walk in prepared, not blindsided.

How to stay the decision-maker

Simple ways to keep control of the choices that shape the next chapter.

How to recognise high-conflict tactics

The common patterns Amy has spent years reporting on, explained in plain language.

How to protect your peace through the process

Habits and boundaries that help women keep their footing before, during and after.

Meet Amy

Hi, I'm Amy Polacko

I'm a divorce and life coach, a journalist and a speaker. I've been through divorce twice myself, and now I help women take their power back before, during and after it.

As a journalist I've written about divorce and women's lives for The Washington Post, The Guardian, HuffPost and Ms. I host the Girl, Wake Up! podcast, co-authored the book FRAMED, and have led a women's divorce retreat at Omega Institute.

The question I hear most, and the honest answer.

Hi [first name],

It's the question I hear most. And it makes sense: you already have one professional, why add another?

An attorney handles the legal work. A coach helps with everything around it: getting organised, preparing for meetings, thinking through decisions, and staying steady when it gets loud. Many women find that makes the time with their attorney more focused.

That's the work I do 1:1. If you want to talk about whether it fits, the application takes two minutes.

"Many women walk in with a head full of worry and no paperwork. The ones who walk in with their documents, accounts and timeline in order get more out of every hour. It isn't hard. It just helps to know the list."

Script 2 · "Coach vs attorney"

Hook (0 to 3s)

"Divorce coach or divorce attorney? Here's the difference."

Body

"An attorney handles the legal work. A coach helps with everything around it: getting organised, preparing for meetings, and thinking through decisions. Knowing who does what can make every legal hour count."

CTA

Shot: talking to camera, split-screen text "Coach" and "Attorney" in blue and red.
